body:
## Problem

Found in PR #598 (#409, the deferred-findings ledger), not yet on main.

`pdca signoff --delta` writes its text verbatim into §9 (`template/src/pdca_harness/cli.py:1466` → `signoff.record`, `signoff.py:247`). Only the flow path flattens it (`flow.py:181-182`). If the pasted text holds a `## 6. NEEDS-HUMAN` heading (for example a §6 block copied from an older SUMMARY), that copy becomes the "last" §6 in the file. `autoiterate.retire_cleared` (`autoiterate.py:348`) reads ticks from it, ignores the real §6, and retires ledger entries the human never cleared.

Reproduced by the issue_409 adversary: a ledger holding `[E1, E2]`, both open in the real §6, then `pdca signoff X --iterate-do --delta "$(printf 'notes\n## 6. NEEDS-HUMAN (from v1)\n- [x] E1\n- [x] E2')"` → both retired (`kept: []`). The test helper `_section6` (`tests/test_autoiterate.py:95-98`) copies the same "last heading" rule, so the suite cannot see it.

## Fix

Flatten `--delta` in `cli._signoff` or in `signoff.record` itself, as `flow.py:181-182` already does.

## Done when

A `--delta` containing a `## 6.` heading cannot change which §6 `retire_cleared` reads. A test pins it on the CLI path.

Raised by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-09-30 (issue_409 §6 row 3 / §10).

comments.body: One symptom of the format design item #607 (milestone 0.70.0). This issue stays as the small, concrete fix in the meantime.

title: signoff --delta is written raw into §9, so a pasted §6 heading makes retire_cleared retire uncleared ledger entries
